text: Sadi Carnot works out the limits on how well heat engines can turn heat into work, laying the groundwork for thermodynamics.
method: Encyclopedia.com biography of Carnot (calls the 1824 work the beginning of thermodynamics)
problem: “Founding thermodynamics” overstates. Carnot’s 1824 book is usually called the beginning of the subject, but it used the wrong caloric theory of heat and the science was built later by Clapeyron, Kelvin and Clausius.

method: History-of-science text on conservation of energy (Mayer 1842, Joule 1843, Helmholtz 1847)
problem: Credit is incomplete. Julius Robert Mayer stated the idea in 1842, before Joule’s 1843 results and Helmholtz’s 1847 essay; histories usually name all three.

text: Two British eclipse expeditions, organized by Frank Dyson and Arthur Eddington, measure starlight bending around the Sun. Eddington’s team observed from Príncipe and another team from Sobral, Brazil. The results support general relativity.
method: Wikipedia (Eddington experiment, via mirror); DOI checked via ADS/Zenodo records of the 1920 paper
problem: Dyson did not lead an expedition. As Astronomer Royal he organized the project with Eddington. Eddington and Cottingham went to Príncipe; Crommelin and Davidson went to Sobral, Brazil.

text: Hubble shows that more distant galaxies are moving away faster, using many speeds measured by Vesto Slipher. Georges Lemaître had predicted this in 1927. It is evidence that the universe is expanding.

sources.cite: Hubble, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 15 (1929)
Cambridge University Press, Renaming Hubble’s Law to the Hubble-Lemaître Law

method: DOI checked via ADS/PMC record; arXiv 1809.02557 and Cambridge University Press article on the IAU 2018 resolution
problem: Credit is incomplete. Georges Lemaître predicted and estimated this relation in 1927, and many of the speeds came from Vesto Slipher’s measurements. The IAU in 2018 recommended the name Hubble–Lemaître law.

text: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain build the first transistor at Bell Labs, in a group led by William Shockley, who soon designed an improved version. All three share the 1956 Nobel Prize. Transistors are the basis of modern electronics.

sources.cite: Computer History Museum, 1947: Invention of the Point-Contact Transistor

method: Computer History Museum Silicon Engine timeline (1947 point-contact transistor; 1948 junction transistor)
problem: The first transistor (December 1947) was built by Bardeen and Brattain. Shockley led the group and invented the junction transistor soon after (1948). All three shared the 1956 Nobel.

text: The US National Ignition Facility achieves fusion ignition (5 December, announced 13 December): the fuel gives off more energy (3.15 MJ) than the laser light that hit it (2.05 MJ). The lasers themselves used far more electricity than that, so it is not yet a power source.

sources.cite: US Department of Energy announcement, December 2022
Physics Today, National Ignition Facility surpasses long-awaited fusion milestone

method: University of California / LLNL release (DOE text) and Physics Today news story (300 MJ grid figure)
problem: “More energy than the lasers put in” is misleading. The shot made 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser light reaching the target, but the lasers drew about 300 MJ from the power grid. Also note the result was announced 13 December.

text: Gave the first clear description of the magnetic compass needle and noticed that it does not point exactly north–south (magnetic declination).
method: Wikipedia Shen Kuo (1031–1095; Dream Pool Essays 1088) and AAAS Scientia article
problem: Small precision fix. Shen Kuo wrote that the needle points south but is always a little east of due south. Saying it does not point exactly north–south matches his words and is still correct.

text: Proved that every continuous symmetry of nature corresponds to a conserved quantity (Noether’s theorem).
method: Colloquium “A Century of Noether’s Theorem” (arXiv 1902.01989); years from standard references
problem: Overstates: the theorem covers continuous symmetries (like shifting in time or space), not every symmetry. Also she worked in the United States from 1933 until her death.
